_doc: [home] The Verdance system: one binary star, the single source of truth for every sky (systems/solar_system.gd SolarSystem.suns_for(planet_id)). star_a is the warm primary (carries shadows), star_b the smaller cooler companion (unshadowed warm fill). size = angular size multiplier (1 = the primary as seen from Verdance), energy = light multiplier; both scale with orbital distance as size / orbit_au and energy / orbit_au^2 (clamped by min_energy / max_energy). Per planet: orbit_au (distance; display order on the solar map), tilt_deg (axial tilt), sep_deg (angular separation of the two suns), sep_angle_deg (direction of the companion from the primary across the sky, 0 = trailing along the sun path, 90 = toward the zenith), day_length_s (game seconds), moons (decorative, owned by each planet env: name, size, color, orbit). Rime is farthest: two small points, weak day light, stars visible by day (day_stars).

globe_day._doc: [v10pace] The clock on a round planet (planet/sky_director.gd, SolarSystem.globe_day(id); a planet's own "globe_day" block overrides single keys). turn_min: minutes for one turn of the planet at speed 1. day_speed / night_speed: how fast the clock runs by day and by night (night = local time before 0.24 or after 0.76, about 48% of a turn), so a full cycle lasts turn_min x (0.52 / day_speed + 0.48 / night_speed) minutes: 36 x (0.743 + 0.253) = 35.8 min, of which 26.7 min day and 9.1 min night (was 24 min: 12.5 day, 11.5 night; owner: 'Sun went down too fast'). start_time: local time (0.5 = noon) when a new game lands. Dawn is local time 0.24, dusk 0.76. A new game lands at 0.32 (morning), so the first dusk comes (0.76 - start_time) x turn_min / day_speed = 22.6 min of play after landing (was 8.2 with Glim found, 13.6 before), the first night lasts 9.1 min and the second dusk comes at 58 min. night_lift_found: how much the night is brightened once Glim is found (0..1; 1 = as bright as the first nights).
